title: The Value of Labors and the Truth of Words
english: When a greater power is being given. Just as those digging into the roots of the earth unearth gold, so those descending into humility bring up virtues. Then the mind feels rest, once having cut off the causes of the passions and being occupied with contemplation; but before this toil, it feels exhaustion and hardship, approaching weakly to the struggle of the opposites.

Chapter 32. The elders most gladly accept a withdrawal occurring by degrees, if anyone has come to this having completed the virtues in communal life; and if he is able to make progress in the withdrawal, let him test himself. But if, being unable, he is diminished in virtue, let him return to the communal life, lest he fall from his senses, being unable to encounter the mechanisms of the thoughts. Just as sons provide consolation to a grieving widow, so also to a soul having fallen, labors provide consolation, which scatter the recognition of the thoughts, and sow the faith of repentance, and proclaim the mercies of Christ, and denounce the committed sins.

We ought, therefore, not to perform labors merely out of habit, but also with a consciousness of thanksgiving, so that the soul might not be found empty of such a philosophy; for if I understand the one giving the ends of the labors in each instance, let us seal it with thanksgiving. Just as a dog sitting by a baby snatches bread, so is an evil thought from the heart lacking understanding. Let us not, therefore, be enticed by the works of the opposites using wickedness, so that we might not hand over the soul to these for plunder. Just as the dance of the stars, bearing light, beautifies the sky, so the truth of the words, bearing a torch, beautifies the man. Let us therefore carry one manner of truth upon the tongue, for the Lord dwells in one way in a house (Psalm 132:1). Just as fierce lightning bolts, having leaped, foretell thunder, so also precise sayings, approaching, signal faith. Let us therefore strive to be faithful to the truth, so that also into the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Love and the Danger of Glory
english: Let us advance in love, the mother-city of virtues. Just as the sun smiles upon the whole earth with its golden rays, so love approaches the soul with all its light-giving operations; if we possess it, we have extinguished the passions and have shone into the heavens. You will perform all toil until you attain holy love, for in its absence, the benefit of present things is nothing. For indeed, anger becomes wild, and characters become harsh, and toils are rendered senseless when mixed with glory. Through the humbling of the soul, David trusted with mourning (Psalm 51:6), and let us also humble the soul through fasting.

Chapter 33. He who practices harshness through bodily toils should not work for praise, nor be puffed up by glory; for in these things the demons agitate the soul; and they strengthen the harshness and the asceticism of the body through glory, and they will pull him toward greater toils so that he may be even more puffed up. For they conspire from within through thoughts, casting these in, saying: Just as one has practiced strictly and has been greatly named, and even after dying he is still spoken of, so also you ascend to the highest height of asceticism, so that you may acquire glory for yourself and your name may become great, even to be spoken of exceedingly after death. Because of those thus deceived, they fight against you not only with bodily toils, but rather they call you into an alliance, because through them they rest in the more difficult toils, for they enthrone him and exalt him toward the teaching word, so that through this he might be praised as one of the first of the great-toilers and the knowers. And they also zealously envy and cast malice against those who are praised for their rectitude, whose practice and knowledge are more wonderful. Even when they painfully put to sleep the burning of his flesh, casting out the impure thoughts from within, so that the spirit of fornication might be thought to have conquered by inheritance, and to match the brightness of the saints, the heart...

title: The Danger of Spiritual Pride and Deception
english: To have become pure, and to have ascended to the edge of holiness. Regarding these things—and the impurities from which he abstained, and the fasts he chose—they assign to him the times in which he ought to boast as an elite, and they diminish the brotherhood as something trivial. Thus, they narrate his struggles as if they were perfected by his own strength alone, saying, ‘I did these things, and I practiced thus, and I was persecuted,’ while even now cutting off the saying, ‘Not I, but the help within me.’ For they do not allow him to confess God as a helper in those things in which they make him magnify himself, so that, having completed all the struggles as if from his own inherent strength, he might fully demand the praise of his labors, so that he might sink into the abyss of blasphemy, unashamedly contradicting by helping himself.

Chapter 34. Thus, indeed, when the heart is echoed by the glory of thoughts and does not oppose them, it will not be outside the possibility of a madness in the secret parts of the mind, with the ruling part of the mind being at risk of being cast out, or through believing in dreams, or being transformed in vigils, or being dazzled by a transformation of light. For Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light to deceive us (2 Cor 11:14), perhaps showing gifts, so that having fallen you might worship, or proclaiming himself to take up the role as another Elijah, or promising to sanctify, some of whom, having received faith in these, missed the truth and became mentally deranged. You then, O suppliant of the Holy Trinity, knowing these things in which you labor, keep your heart with every guard, lest, attending only to external labors, you be bitterly drenched from within. My words, then, O child, are spoken to you, and let your heart keep my sayings; remember Christ who guards you, and let him not forget the worshiper and the consubstantial Trinity, to whom is the glory forever. Amen.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
